newsitem.title: TURKEY: France supports Turkey's human rights promises.
newsitem.headline: France supports Turkey's human rights promises.

text.p: France supported a Turkish pledge to clean up its record on human rights, France's minister for European affairs Michel Barnier said on Monday.
"You can trust France's concrete support...I see these projects as very important steps in the right direction," Barnier told reporters after meeting Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller in Ankara.
He referred to remarks made by Ciller during their meeting to discuss Ankara's human rights reform measures.

Ciller announced last week Turkey would cut the period of detention in custody -- a time rights activists say most police abuse occurs -- and make changes to the State Security Court system, though she gave few details.
Suspects held under anti-terror laws can now be detained for up to a month in 10 emergency rule provinces in the mainly Kurdish southeast and two weeks in the rest of Turkey.
"As well as decreasing the period of detention, we have begun wide-range studies on human rights," Ciller said after the meeting.
She stressed the Turkey's goal of becoming a full member of European Union, saying her country can not accept lagging behind East European countries for full membership.

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said earlier in Paris that Turkey's right promises were in the right direction towards a hoped-for re-establishment of good relations between Turkey and Europe.

Amnesty International launched a worldwide campaign this month to highlight abuses in Turkey, including extrajudicial killings, torture and disappearances. Amnesty has criticised Turkey for failing to live up to previous promises to stamp out rights violations.
The European Parliament last month threatened to hold back hundreds of millions of dollars in European Union aid to Turkey, partly because of its rights record.
